 Yakin gets a laugh with his comment on the field
 00:40 The Swiss national team is just one point away from returning to League A of the Nations League. Will Embolo immediately return to the starting lineup in Slovenia? And what’s the condition of the field in Maribor? Here’s what Murat Yakin has to say.
 Jan Arnet , Jörg Christen, Maribor 
 12.11.2026, 20:03 • Today at 07:07 Here's what it's all about
 Promotion to League A of the Nations League is within Switzerland's grasp. On Friday, a draw in Slovenia would be enough for the Swiss national team to seal the deal.
 However, Murat Yakin will have to do without Johan Manzambi in Maribor. In his place, Breel Embolo is expected to return to the starting lineup, as the Swiss national team coach hinted the day before the game.
 Fabian Rieder is likely to play the Manzambi role and start at the ten, even though he also feels “very comfortable” playing at the six.
 Summary created with With impressive performances in September and October and four wins in their first four games, Switzerland has put itself in an excellent position in the Nations League. With just one point still needed ahead of the upcoming matches against Slovenia and Scotland, they are on the verge of achieving their major goal: direct promotion back to League A of the Nations League. The Swiss national team aims to seal the deal as early as Friday in Maribor.
 The game was originally supposed to take place in Ljubljana, but had to be moved to Maribor due to poor field conditions. “We watched NK Maribor’s last home game online beforehand, and I was glad to see a green field. I also took a quick look at it earlier, and it looks good,” Murat Yakin replied at the press conference the day before the game when asked about the field—and drew laughter: “Tomorrow’s motto might be: Play flat, win big!”
 Embolo Set to Return to the Starting Lineup
 In the absence of Granit Xhaka and Breel Embolo, their replacements, Ardon Jashari and Zeki Amdouni, shone during the last training camp. Since Xhaka is once again out with an injury, Jashari is likely to get another chance as the playmaker, even though he still hasn’t moved beyond a reserve role at Milan.
 Up front, the situation is different: Embolo is back, and there’s little reason to think he won’t return to the starting lineup right away on Friday. Amdouni, who was in such great form last fall, just made his comeback this past weekend after recovering from an ankle injury. Winsley Boteli’s recent performances for Sion haven’t done much to earn him a spot in the starting lineup, nor have Cedric Itten’s for Werder Bremen.
 “Zeki did a great job of following our instructions last time, but then, unfortunately, he got injured. In practice, you can see that he’s regained his full confidence. After four weeks, though, he still needs to get back into the rhythm during games,” says Yakin, hinting that Embolo will likely be the one to start: “Breel is in top form, scores regularly, and is in a rhythm. I’m glad to have two such good forwards.”
 Manzambi is out—will Rieder play at the ten?
 The national team coach will certainly be forced to make a change in attacking midfield. On Thursday morning, it becomes clear that Johan Manzambi has to leave the camp due to calf problems. Fabian Rieder would be the logical choice for the number 10 position.
 “At Augsburg, I play as a defensive midfielder and feel very comfortable there. But the situation with the national team is different, and I really enjoy playing as an attacking midfielder there,” says Rieder, who has most recently been playing primarily on the right wing. On the wing, Michel Aebischer could return to the starting lineup.
 01:11 Rieder: «Ich versuche, meine Erfahrung den Jungen mitzugeben»
 There’s also a question mark on the left side of the defense. Ricardo Rodriguez was sidelined by injury for four weeks with his club, Torino, but he’s now with the national team nonetheless. The 34-year-old already proved back in September that he doesn’t need much playing time to be ready. Rodriguez is “ready,” but “will likely not start,” says the Swiss national team coach. Sascha Britschgi is on standby as an alternative.
 Yakin Has His Sights Set on Petkovic's Record
 For Yakin, this will be his 70th game on the Swiss national team’s sidelines. This ties him with Köbi Kuhn and brings him ever closer to Vladimir Petkovic’s record (78 games). “I’m proud of this milestone, but right now, the only thing that matters to me is tomorrow’s game,” he says. “How many more games I’ll coach depends on the results. In any case, I’m looking forward to every future game as the Swiss national team’s coach.”
 Switzerland's possible lineup in Slovenia: 
Kobel; Athekame, Elvedi, Akanji, Britschgi; Jashari, Freuler, Aebischer, Rieder, Ndoye; Embolo.
